implementation_state: Persistence and ownership exist: AppState owns an AccountStore behind the optional account feature, and the registry is configuration on ProviderConfig. Execution exists as account::reconcile, which probes declared accounts through a dyn shim and publishes into the store — including on failure, so a stale healthy reading cannot masquerade as current. Two further account-owned surfaces have since been added: a provider-neutral observation layer (ObservedResourceEvent, ResourceEffect, ObservedProviderAccounting) with a bounded AccountEventLog, and a maintenance block on AccountConfig carrying the check-in declaration. The node stays PARTIAL for exactly the reason it was, and that reason is unchanged: execution is not integrated. No call site invokes the reconciler, no credential-resolution path feeds it, and the maintenance block has no scheduler — checkin_enabled and checkin_interval_secs are declared, validated and read by a manual Tauri command, and nothing in the product fires on a timer, so every check-in today is one a person started. The observation layer has the same shape of gap: written, fixture-tested, and held by nothing, so no observed resource event reaches a consumer. It would be easy to read the added surface as progress toward integration and it is not; the parts are proven and the wiring is absent. The record previously claimed persistence and ownership did not exist; it corrected the record, not the code. See E-119, E-130, E-131, E-132.
required_gates: Generic account types and pure calculations
unblock_condition: Satisfied. Stage 5 is revalidated at E-133, the owned persistence and runtime contract shipped at E-119, and ML feature order is untouched: default remains ["ml"]. Why the status still does not move on that basis is stated in the notes, because it is a distinction and not a formality.
notes: Check-in is the second account-owned execution surface and is the only one a person can currently reach. The reconciler still has no caller, and the resource-event log has no consumer; neither is wired, and the maintenance declaration has no scheduler behind it.

ALL THREE OF THIS NODE'S GATES ARE NOW MET and none of them is about integration, which is the whole reason blocked_by can be empty while the status is PARTIAL. OBSERVABILITY is the precedent for the opposite conclusion and it was not followed here, because the two cases differ in one respect that matters: observability is unreachable from the product deliberately and 7F owns its real-traffic use, whereas account::reconcile is unreachable because nothing calls it and no successor node owns that work either. A deliberate handoff is a gate satisfied; an unowned gap is not. A reader who disagrees with that reading has a reasonable case and the argument is here rather than hidden in the absence of an explanation.
